original_interpretation: WSTS statistics include estimates made by WSTS for semiconductor companies that do not participate in the survey, so the published world total is not purely member-reported data.
evidence_found: "The statistics presented in this report have been compiled on the basis of confidential data submitted by companies participating in the survey; estimates provided by WSTS, Inc. are included for nonparticipating companies worldwide." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 2, Program Overview, dated 01/30/2019)

original_interpretation: WSTS states that it adds estimates for non-participants wherever its membership covers less than 100% of a market segment, because it aims to represent the entire semiconductor market.
evidence_found: "As WSTS attempts to represent the entire semiconductor market in its reports, estimates are added for non-participants in cases where the WSTS membership covers less than 100% of the respective market segment." (wsts.org, Basic Principles of Data Collection and Report Generation page, accessed 2026-09-30)

original_interpretation: When a participating WSTS member fails to submit data for a month, the data collection agents impute its input using that company's previously reported market share.
evidence_found: "To adjust for non-receipt of any participant's data, Moss Adams LLP, topserve.ch GmbH and Grant Thornton Taiyo (GTT) will use that company's previously reported market share to compute its input data for the current month." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 2, Program Overview, dated 01/30/2019)
notes: Procedure as described in the 2018 Green Book (published Jan 2019); the named agents may have changed since.

original_interpretation: WSTS statistics cover non-captive semiconductor manufacturers only; chips made by a company solely for its own use are outside the stated reporting population.
evidence_found: "The report reflects worldwide statistics for all non-captive semiconductor manufacturers worldwide." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 2, Program Overview, dated 01/30/2019); same page: "Reported data include all monthly net billings (shipments) between semiconductor manufacturers and their end customers, authorized distributors and divisions or subsidiaries that manufacture end products." and "comparable market prices for internal transfers"
correction: The exclusion is at the manufacturer level (purely captive manufacturers are outside the population). Chips that a non-captive manufacturer transfers to its own end-product divisions ARE counted, valued at comparable market prices (see CLM-0579). 'Chips made by a company solely for its own use' should be read as 'chips from manufacturers that make chips only for their own use'.

original_interpretation: WSTS reports monthly net billings (shipments) from semiconductor manufacturers to end customers, authorised distributors, and divisions or subsidiaries that make end products.
evidence_found: "Reported data include all monthly net billings (shipments) between semiconductor manufacturers and their end customers, authorized distributors and divisions or subsidiaries that manufacture end products." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 2, Program Overview, dated 01/30/2019)

original_interpretation: Distributor resale is not counted a second time in the WSTS market: a chip sold through a distributor enters once, at the manufacturer's billing price to the distributor, so the WSTS total excludes distributor margins.
evidence_found: Definition supporting the reading: "Reported data include all monthly net billings (shipments) between semiconductor manufacturers and their end customers, authorized distributors and divisions or subsidiaries that manufacture end products." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 2, Program Overview, dated 01/30/2019). No passage mentions distributor resale explicitly.
notes: Checked as an interpretation: the reporting population is manufacturers' billings only, so distributor resale value (and margin) is outside scope by definition. WSTS does not state this in words; the conclusion follows from the definition. Confidence stays low by rule for interpretations.

original_interpretation: WSTS assigns every billing to a region by the customer's shipment (ship-to) location, not by the seller's headquarters or where the chip was made.
evidence_found: "All billings are reported according to customer shipment location." (p. 2); Definitions, Geographic Billing: "Dollar value of net billings into each region by ship-to location between non-captive semconductor manufacturers and their end customers, authorized distributors and divisions or subsidiaries that manufacture end products." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 3)
notes: Definition as of the 2018 Green Book (Jan 2019). The 'not by seller HQ or fab location' part is implied by the ship-to rule rather than stated.

original_interpretation: WSTS values billings at actual sales prices, and internal transfers (e.g. to a manufacturer's own end-product divisions) at comparable market prices.
evidence_found: "Actual sales prices (or comparable market prices for internal transfers) are used to value all billings." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 2, Program Overview, dated 01/30/2019); Definitions, Price: "Actual sales price or comparable market price for internal transfers." (p. 3)

original_interpretation: WSTS billings include non-recurring engineering (NRE) charges.
evidence_found: Definitions, Bill: "Shipments made and billed by ship-to location, including NRE." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 3)

original_interpretation: WSTS monthly statistics (2018 Green Book) were compiled by three data collection agents: Moss Adams LLP (Campbell), topserve.ch GmbH (Winterthur) and Grant Thornton Taiyo (Tokyo), which tabulated member data without audit.
evidence_found: Cover: "Compiled by Moss Adams LLP in Campbell, topserve.ch GmbH in Winterthur and Grant ThorntonTaiyo in Tokyo" (p. 1); "Because their work was limited to tabulating information furnished without audit, they can assume no responsibility for the accuracy of the underlying amounts." (p. 2)

original_interpretation: The names of companies participating in the WSTS survey and the public sources used for its non-participant estimates are disclosed only to participants, via the WSTS Administrator, not publicly.
evidence_found: "All participant inquiries with respect to the program, including the name of companies participating in the survey and the public sources used in compiling estimates, should be directed to the WSTS Administrator." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 2, Program Overview, dated 01/30/2019)
correction: The source only says participants should direct inquiries about participant names and estimate sources to the WSTS Administrator. It does not say these are withheld from the public. That the member list is not public is the researcher's observation (no list on the WSTS pages opened), not a WSTS statement.

original_interpretation: Public inquiries about WSTS data are handled by SIA for the Americas, Taiwan and China, by ESIA in Europe, by the WSTS Japan Council in Japan and by KSIA for the rest of Asia Pacific.
evidence_found: "All public inquiries concerning WSTS should be addressed to SIA in the Americas, Taiwan and China, to ESIA in Europe, to WSTS Japan Council in Japan and to KSIA in Asia Pacific (except for Taiwan and China)." (Green Book 2018 sample, p. 2, Program Overview, dated 01/30/2019)
notes: As of the 2018 Green Book (Jan 2019); the Introduction page (2026) mentions '5 regional distribution channels for WSTS data to non-members', so channel arrangements may have changed.

original_interpretation: WSTS states it has 50 member companies.
evidence_found: "WSTS Key Data 50 Member companies 4 Regional organizations 5 regional distribution channels for WSTS data to non-members 40 years of statistical data 4 years forecast updated twice a year" (wsts.org Introduction to WSTS page, Key Data sidebar, accessed 2026-09-30)
notes: Self-reported, correctly typed reported_claim. The page has no date for the figure (footer copyright 1998-2024 / 2005-2026).

original_interpretation: WSTS publishes a consensus market forecast twice a year covering four years, produced from member companies' submitted outlooks and adjusted at a members' 'forecast meeting'.
evidence_found: "4 years forecast updated twice a year" (Introduction to WSTS, Key Data); "Member companies provide their perception of the market development over the following 4 years to WSTS. WSTS applies statistical methods to the received forecast inputs and presents the conclusion to the Committee (the assembly of all member companies) for a final review and adjustment in the so called \"forecast meeting\". ... a consensus forecast that is published by WSTS twice a year (spring and autumn)." (Basic Principles page)
notes: Presentation (SRC-0226, slide 7) adds structure: 2 years quarterly plus 2 years annually.

original_interpretation: WSTS member companies enter monthly unit and revenue data online; regional data collection agents check and anonymise them and a worldwide agent aggregates the totals, with data published within about five weeks of month end.
evidence_found: "Individual semiconductor member companies enter unit sales and revenue data into a simple online form monthly. Data-collection agents (DCA) in the regions compile information from the companies. They check the data for completeness, consistency, and plausibility ... The data getting anonymized. Our worldwide DCA receives the regional data, further checks the information for consistency, aggregates totals, and prepares statistical report." (slide 8); "published within five weeks of the closing of the month to the subscribers" (slide 2)
notes: The five-week lag applies to subscriber publication (WSTS self-description).

original_interpretation: WSTS added new wide-bandgap (SiC and GaN) product categories for power transistors and rectifiers in 2023/2024.
evidence_found: "For instance, WSTS introduced in 2023/2024 new wide bandgap product categories (SiC / GaN) for power transistors & rectifiers." (WSTS subscription presentation Oct 2024, slide 5)

original_interpretation: Companies acting as foundries cannot join WSTS as regular members and may instead take a 'foundry membership' subscription.
evidence_found: "Semiconductor Manufacturers who cannot join WSTS as Member for whatever reason (e.g. acting as a foundry) may enter a subscription with a foundry membership with WSTS. Note that this option is only available to Semiconductor Manufacturers." (wsts.org Subscription with WSTS - Foundry membership page, accessed 2026-09-30)
notes: The page gives foundry status as an example ('for whatever reason (e.g. acting as a foundry)'), which implies but does not state a blanket rule that all foundries are barred from regular membership.

original_interpretation: Because WSTS records billings of non-captive chip vendors at the point of sale to customers, and foundries are not reporting members, foundry wafer revenue is not a separate layer of the WSTS total; the value of foundry-made chips enters once, through the fabless or IDM vendor's own sale price.
evidence_found: Premises checked: foundry page: "Semiconductor Manufacturers who cannot join WSTS as Member for whatever reason (e.g. acting as a foundry) may enter a subscription with a foundry membership"; membership sidebar: "A company that at least designs and sells semiconductor products under its own trade name may become WSTS member."; Green Book p. 2: "worldwide statistics for all non-captive semiconductor manufacturers" and billings "between semiconductor manufacturers and their end customers, authorized distributors and divisions or subsidiaries that manufacture end products."
correction: Premises verified, but the conclusion is not stated by WSTS. Caveat: WSTS also adds estimates for non-participants to 'represent the entire semiconductor market' (SRC-0228), and no public text says whether foundry wafer sales are excluded from those estimates. The inference is plausible, not confirmed.

original_interpretation: The free WSTS Historical Billings Report gives monthly billings and three-month moving averages by four regions (Americas, Europe, Japan, Asia Pacific) from 1986, drawn from the WSTS Blue Book; the July 2026 edition had data to July 2026.
evidence_found: Download page: "Four decades of WSTS statistics from the WSTS Blue Book are now available for free download - with latest data from July 2026 . No login is required. The tables are in MS Excel and PDF format and provide monthly data, as well as three months moving averages for total semiconductor revenues by the four regions Americas, Europe, Japan and Asia Pacific." XLSX: header "1986 to Date", "All numbers are in 1000 US$.", first year block 1986; the last populated month is July 2026 (Worldwide 142,480,424; Aug 2026 empty).
notes: The XLSX header also still reads '36 Years WSTS Blue Book Data' and '(c) 2025', although the file runs to July 2026.

original_interpretation: The free WSTS historical dataset contains regional totals only; annual product-category splits (discretes, optoelectronics, sensors, analog, micro, logic, memory) back to 1986 are not in it and are only public for recent years via forecast releases.
evidence_found: XLSX shared-string table (both sheets) holds only: Worldwide, Americas, Europe, Japan, Asia Pacific, month names, Q1-Q4, "Total Year", "3 Months Moving Averages", unit lines, the title and copyright line. No product-category labels.
correction: Verified that the free XLSX has regional totals only, with no product categories. The added statement that annual product splits back to 1986 are 'only public for recent years via forecast releases' is not supported by SRC-0223 or SRC-0224. The companion free PDF ('Monthly data - 3MMA') was not checked. The subscriber 'Blue Book History' is described as covering data since 1991 (SRC-0229).

original_interpretation: The free WSTS historical dataset does not split out China; China is included in 'Asia Pacific', although WSTS monthly subscriber statistics report China as a separate region.
evidence_found: XLSX regions: only "Americas", "Europe", "Japan", "Asia Pacific", "Worldwide"; Worldwide equals the sum of the four (e.g. 1986: 8,508,557 + 5,343,763 + 10,450,725 + 2,052,314 = 26,355,359 thousand US$). SIA July 2026 release (SRC-0008): "Regionally, year-to-year sales in July were up in the Americas (171.3%), Asia Pacific/All Other (134.9%), China (123.6%), Europe (85.2%), and Japan (50.8%)." ... "Monthly sales are compiled by the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS)"
correction: Verified that the free dataset has no separate China region and that WSTS-sourced monthly data are published with China separate (SIA release). That China sits inside 'Asia Pacific' in the free file is deduced from Worldwide = sum of four regions; no WSTS text opened states it in words.
notes: Minor conflicting signal: the WSTS Foundry-membership page (SRC-0229) describes the subscriber Blue Book regional split as 'Americas, Europe, Japan and Asia Pacific' (four regions), which may be an out-of-date description.

original_interpretation: WSTS Blue Book data put the 1986 worldwide semiconductor market at US$26.4 billion.
evidence_found: XLSX sheet 1 ("All numbers are in 1000 US$."), year block 1986, row "Worldwide", column N "Total Year": 26355359 (re-parsed independently from the downloaded July 2026 file).
notes: 26.355 USD bn nominal; matches the metric value. Later-vintage (July 2026) Blue Book figure; contemporaneous releases may differ.
